items.author: DjaniWhaleSkul
items.context: @DjaniWhaleSkul (9.619 seguidores, en inglés): recibió un email que dice que hardware wallets como BitBox exigirán KYC obligatorio en Suiza (citando DAC8/OCDE) o dejarán de funcionar; concluye que es phishing, que su email se filtró y menciona los ataques físicos a holders en Francia. Noticia/alerta fresca (~24 min), cuenta mediana, 3 respuestas: encaja con custodia y filtraciones de datos.
items.suggested_text:
You read it right: it's phishing. A hardware wallet has no account to suspend. The keys live on the device, signing happens offline, and no vendor or regulator can switch that off remotely. Any email saying your wallet "stops working" unless you complete KYC is describing something the device physically can't do.

The real risk is the one you pointed at: the purchase record. Ledger's 2020 e-commerce leak exposed names, phone numbers and home addresses of 270k+ customers, and the phishing and threats that followed never really stopped. The keys were never touched; the shipping database was the weak point.

Self-custody has two layers that rarely get discussed together: protecting the seed, and protecting the fact that you hold one at all. Most setups only solve the first.

The full air-gapped process is here: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526
